text:
Sam Irwin: Heads up — customer on private VPC deployment reported intermittent 502s when hitting our hosted-compatible API through their ILB. Reports started ~08:10 UTC. Also they say audit logs for last 24h are missing on our side. Suspect egress/firewall.
Ria Martin: thanks. can you paste the failing request id + stack traces? also which customer/org id?
Sam Irwin: org=acme-energy, req ids: req_0a9f3b6d, req_4c2d1e00. Here's proxy error snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T08:11:02Z] proxy -> runtime: dial tcp 10.0.3.7:443: i/o timeout
runtime: upstream response 502
```
They're on aws us-west-2, private deployment (customer-managed VPC) with our private control plane. They said they did a "default deny" firewall policy last week.
Matt Zhou: i/o timeout to 10.0.3.7:443 — that's our KMS proxy in private cluster? Could be NAT or SG blocking. Can they reach kms.redwood-internal:443 from worker nodes? ask them to run `curl -v https://kms.redwood-internal:443/health` from a node.
Elaine Park: also confirm the audit-log forwarder (fluentd) can reach our log-collector endpoint (logs.redwood-internal:5044). Missing audit logs usually from blocked egress to 10.32.200.0/22 (collector subnet) or blocked TLS to collector's port.
Sam Irwin: I asked for these checks. Customer ran a quick test and got `curl: (28) Operation timed out`. They also shared `iptables -L` showing default DROP on OUTPUT. They prefer default-deny. 
Security Bot: ALERT: KMS handshake failed for acme-energy at 2026-03-16T08:11:02Z — tls error: remote handshake timeout. Logged as SEC-2026-03-ACME-010.
Ria Martin: ok, likely egress rules missing for our control plane endpoints + kms/hsm. Need minimal outbound allowlist: kms.redwood-internal:443, logs.redwood-internal:5044, metadata endpoints for cloud provider (e.g., 169.254.169.254), and time sync (ntp). Also HSM-let if they use customer HSM -> make sure outgoing to hsm-host:23364 allowed.
Matt Zhou: repro steps for our internal ops: from a worker node with default deny, run:
```
curl -w '\\n%{http_code}\\n' -sS -D - https://kms.redwood-internal:443/health || echo KMS unreachable
nc -vz logs.redwood-internal 5044 || echo logs unreachable
```
If both fail, add SG outbound allow to those FQDNs or add NAT gateway with FQDN egress.
Elaine Park: FYI — audit retention question from customer: they want 365d retention for audit logs. Our Private plan default is 90d. We told support this needs enterprise add-on; logged with acct mgmt.
Sam Irwin: customer also reported billing anomalies (overage charges) when our retries fired due to timeouts. They want immediate rollback/credits. Can billing team flag `acme-energy` for review? @matt-ops can you open billing ticket?
Matt Zhou: opened internal ticket BILL-8372, pinging finance. For immediate mitigation ask customer to add temporary outbound allow rules to their firewall for the endpoints above. 
Ria Martin: also verifying KMS key access — need to check that our control plane's service account IPs are allowed in their HSM ACLs. If they use customer-managed HSM, IP whitelisting often blocks new control-plane nodes when autoscaling.
Sam Irwin: customer ran a quick fix: allowed outbound to kms.redwood-internal:443 and logs.redwood-internal:5044 => API success returned, audit logs started appearing. They kept default-deny but added those two egress rules.
Security Bot: RESOLVED: SEC-2026-03-ACME-010 — KMS handshake failures resolved after outbound allowlist. Auto-close in 24h if no regressions.
Elaine Park: follow-up: we'll add a KB doc for Private/VPC minimal egress policy (kms, logs, ntp, metadata, ocsp) and a templated iptables / security-group snippet. Assign me for KB draft.
Sam Irwin: attaching repro notes and commands above to the support ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
